newsitem.title: USA: Agriculture official indicted in Espy probe.
newsitem.headline: Agriculture official indicted in Espy probe.

text.p: A federal grand jury Tuesday indicted a senior Agriculture Department official based in Mississippi as part of the investigation of former Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy, the prosecutor in the Espy case said.
Norris Faust was indicted on three counts of lying to a federal grand jury in August, Independent Counsel Donald Smaltz said in a statement.
Faust, 46, is the Executive Director for Mississippi of the Agriculture Department's Farm Service Agency, the statement said.

The indictment alleged that Faust signed an order eliminating a regulation that would have affected a claim by Mississippi farmer and Espy political supporter Brooke Keith Mitchell to obtain farm subsidies.
Last week Mitchell and his Five M Farming Enterprises firm pleaded guilty to illegally conspiring to collect government farm payments.
In September, Sun-Diamond Growers of California, the largest U.S. fruit cooperative, was convicted on eight counts of courting Espy's favor by giving him illegal gifts.
Espy resigned as Agriculture Secretary at the end of 1994 amid charges that he illegally took favors from companies and agricultural concerns that the Agriculture Department regulated.
